shared_elements: low-relief carving on a flat/columnar stone surface
dense rows of small script-like signs arranged in horizontal registers
human-derived imagery (figures in A; possible glyph faces in B)
justification: Both surfaces carry low-relief carving that includes a field of small repeated script-like signs laid out in horizontal rows, which is the only real correspondence. A shows large standing human figures in profile, one facing another with raised hand and held objects, occupying most of the field, whereas B shows no figural scene at all, only stacked blocks of rounded glyphic signs wrapping a columnar surface, and the sign forms and figural conventions are wholly unlike.
